name: Malicious Cable Detector by O.MG
one_line: Inline dongle: plug a suspect USB cable into it, then into a host port. Samples the cable's power draw 200,000 times/sec and uses side-channel power analysis to flag known malicious cables including O.MG Cables, which show nothing on the data lines until triggered; also blocks the data lines so the port-side device can charge safely.
why_notable: Purpose-built defensive counter-tool for BadUSB cable implants; nothing equivalent is tracked. NOTE price varies by seller: $40 Hak5, $60 and $74.52 elsewhere.

name: O.MG Programmer USB A+C
one_line: USB dongle for initial provisioning, firmware updates, recovery after self-destruct, and forensic dumps/backups of any O.MG Cable, Plug, Adapter or UnBlocker; one programmer covers the whole family.
why_notable: The required tool for reflashing and forensically imaging the O.MG implant line - not a cable, case or sticker.

name: O.MG Cable, Woven (Elite, USB-C/USB-C)
one_line: Same Elite O.MG Cable electronics as the base model; the outer jacket is braided fabric instead of TPE plastic. USB-C to USB-C, directional connector only.
why_notable: Jacket/SKU variant flagged New on the site. Treat as a note on the existing O.MG Cable record, not a new device, unless a hardware revision is confirmed.

name: Glytch GPS Mod for Pager
one_line: 3D-printed hand-assembled add-on carrying a Quectel LC86 multi-constellation GNSS chipset that clips onto the WiFi Pineapple Pager to geotag its Wi-Fi survey and attack logs.
why_notable: Own chipset and SKU, adds a sensor the base Pager lacks. Seen at $79 and $85.32 at other sellers.

name: Glytch Mesh Mod for Pager
one_line: 3D-printed add-on with an 868/900 MHz radio and integrated antenna that clips onto the WiFi Pineapple Pager for sub-GHz mesh networking.
why_notable: Adds off-grid mesh comms to an already-tracked device. Seen at $79 and $85.32 elsewhere.

name: Glytch Ethernet Mod for Pager
one_line: 3D-printed add-on using an RTL8152B USB-to-Ethernet chip to give the WiFi Pineapple Pager a wired RJ45 port.
why_notable: Stock USB-Ethernet controller with no security-specific circuitry - closer to the generic-adapter exclusion than the other two Glytch mods. Recommend dropping.

name: ChipWhisperer-HuskyPlus
one_line: Side-channel capture and glitching board: 250 MS/s 12-bit ADC, Artix-7A100T FPGA with a 327,828-sample buffer, programmable clock and voltage glitch injection, logic-analyzer triggering on pattern match, UART or ARM trace.
why_notable: Distinct higher-spec SKU above the tracked Husky - larger FPGA and buffer, different price tier.

name: ChipSHOVER
one_line: Motorized 3-axis XYZ positioning stage, 5 cm travel per axis, better than 200 nm precision and 4 um repeatability, for placing EM fault-injection probes or side-channel sensors over a die; driven from an LCD panel or Python.
why_notable: New product category for NewAE - a precision robotic positioner for chip-level probing.

name: CW310 Bergen Board (Large FPGA, K410T)
one_line: FPGA target board around a Xilinx Kintex K410T with a supervisory MCU for config/temp/voltage/clock control, DDR3+SRAM, JTAG/USB/PMOD headers, multi-stage VCC-INT filtering with inductive shunt and LNA for power analysis, and SMA/fan access for EM fault injection.
why_notable: Large-FPGA target for full SoC/crypto-core emulation in side-channel research. Out of stock (supply chain).

name: PhyWhisperer-USB (CW610)
one_line: In-line USB 2.0 LS/FS/HS monitor and trigger box with a Spartan FPGA and 240 MHz clock; buffers 8,192 bytes, fires a cycle-accurate trigger on matched data patterns, has a power shunt and front-panel power-cycle button, and feeds sync clock/trigger to ChipWhisperer capture hardware.
why_notable: Returned by both the NewAE and Crowd Supply surveys at different prices - $360 direct, $365 on Crowd Supply. Times power-analysis and fault-injection captures against USB targets.

name: CW308 UFO Board
one_line: Baseboard providing shared 1.2-3.5V supplies, an oscillator/crystal socket, on-board filtering for clean power measurement and diode-protected I/O for voltage glitching, accepting swappable 8-bit, 32-bit and FPGA target daughtercards.
why_notable: The standard target platform for ChipWhisperer side-channel and glitching work. Listed out of stock.

name: CW312T-RP2350
one_line: Target board carrying a Raspberry Pi RP2350 (dual-core ARM + RISC-V) with an external regulator bypassing the chip's internal one, for power analysis and fault-injection/glitch-detector testing.
why_notable: Standalone target board for a current, widely used MCU family (Pico 2).

name: SAM4S CW313 Target
one_line: Target board with a populated Microchip ATSAM4S2 (Cortex-M4, 128KB flash, 64KB SRAM, 1.2V core) programmable by serial bootloader or JTAG, for running crypto code under power and fault analysis. Requires a CW313 baseboard.
why_notable: Populated MCU target sold as its own SKU.

name: NewAE Probe Set with Power Supply
one_line: Isolated power module (5V USB in, +3.3V for LNA, +/-7.8V for the differential probe, up to 50V isolation) sold with a differential probe, an LNA probe and an H-field probe for measuring power and EM signals off a chip.
why_notable: Physical EM and power probes not covered by any tracked capture board; closer to sensing accessories than a standalone instrument.

name: Socket Target for CW308 (STM32F-SOCKET64)
one_line: CW308 daughtercard with an empty TQFP-64 ZIF socket and a switch selecting two pinouts, for socketing user-supplied STM32F chips for side-channel and glitch testing without soldering. No MCU included.
why_notable: Bare socket/adapter card for the CW308 ecosystem - borderline against the generic-adapter exclusion.

name: Opera Cake for HackRF
one_line: Add-on board routing two SMA ports to any of eight secondary antenna/filter ports (1x8 or dual 1x4), 1 MHz-4 GHz, switchable by frequency or time from existing HackRF software such as hackrf_sweep.
why_notable: The only currently sold GSG accessory adding automated multi-antenna/filter-bank switching to HackRF. GSG lists no prices; $190 from a reseller, also seen at $205.20.

name: URTI (Universal Radio Test Instrument)
one_line: In-development wideband full-duplex SDR with an integrated directional coupler, intended to act as spectrum analyzer, VNA, vector signal generator/analyzer, antenna analyzer, power meter and frequency counter in one device.
why_notable: Open-source GSG project (ARDC/TAPR funded) with a live product page, no price and no release. Needs a status check before listing.

name: ChipWhisperer Pro (CW1200)
one_line: Higher-tier ChipWhisperer capture unit. Datasheet and older docs exist but it no longer appears on NewAE's current store or ChipWhisperer product page.
why_notable: APPEARS DISCONTINUED, superseded by Husky/HuskyPlus. Worth adding with status discontinued rather than omitting, since people still own and resell these.

name: CW305 Artix FPGA Target Board
one_line: Artix-7 FPGA target board for side-channel analysis against crypto cores implemented in FPGA logic.
why_notable: APPEARS DISCONTINUED - product URL now 404s, seemingly superseded by the CW310. Same recommendation: list as discontinued.

name: SD Sniffer
one_line: Passive interposer PCB inserting between a full-size SD card and its host socket, breaking out the SPI/SD bus lines to a header so a logic analyzer or MCU can passively capture card-to-host traffic.
why_notable: SparkFun's own copy says the tap is for use 'whether for hacking or debugging'. Cheap purpose-sold interposer for SD-based embedded and forensic targets.

name: SparkFun microSD Sniffer
one_line: Same interposer concept sized for microSD: exposes the SPI bus between a microSD card and its socket on an 8-pin header for external capture.
why_notable: Relevant to intercepting microSD traffic in cameras, dashcams and IoT devices during hardware-hacking or forensic work.

name: RTL-SDR Blog V3 USB Dongle with Dipole Antenna Kit
one_line: USB SDR receiver (RTL2832U + R820T2, roughly 500kHz-1.7GHz) bundled with a dipole antenna kit; the prior hardware revision of the RTL-SDR Blog line. Backordered at SparkFun.
why_notable: Earlier revision of the tracked V4.

name: Diabolic Drive
one_line: USB flash-drive-shaped device behaving as normal 64GB storage until wirelessly commanded over Wi-Fi to expose a HID keyboard interface and inject a stored payload; spoofs VID/PID/serial for both the storage and HID personas.
why_notable: Combines real flash storage, remote-triggered HID injection and hardware-ID spoofing in one drive.

name: Diabolic Parasite
one_line: Inline USB implant: the target's keyboard or mouse plugs into the Parasite's female port and the Parasite into the freed host port. Clones the passthrough device's hardware identity, logs keystrokes to a web UI, and wirelessly triggers injection with randomized typing cadence and ALT+Numpad layout bypass.
why_notable: Passive keylogging, identity cloning and remote injection in one covert implant.

name: OpticSpy
one_line: Photodiode receiver module converting visible and near-IR optical signals into a digital serial stream over USB, for finding and decoding optical covert channels, blinkenlight data exfiltration and IR remote signals.
why_notable: TEMPEST-style optical covert-channel discovery - a niche nothing tracked covers.

name: HydraLink
one_line: USB 3.0 to Automotive Ethernet (100BASE-T1 / 1000BASE-T1) adapter appearing as a native Ethernet interface, letting Wireshark, Scapy, tcpdump and bridge-utils sniff, bridge and manipulate in-vehicle Ethernet such as SOME/IP and DoIP at wire speed.
why_notable: Every other automotive tool found is CAN-focused; this covers the Ethernet layer of modern vehicles.

name: GGtag
one_line: RP2040 e-paper badge emulating 125kHz RFID tags (ASK and FSK), programmed over USB serial, a web-serial browser interface, or audio via ggwave; 3.52-inch e-paper display.
why_notable: Novel form factor for RFID tag emulation - not a Proxmark/Chameleon/Flipper-style reader.

name: ESP32JTAG
one_line: Wi-Fi-connected JTAG/SWD debug probe combining an ESP32 with an onboard FPGA, a 16-channel 250MHz logic analyzer, FPGA bitstream programming and a UART terminal, all through a built-in web server with no drivers.
why_notable: Wireless multi-function debug probe; the tracked Tigard, Glasgow and Bus Pirate are all wired USB.

name: ProxmarkPro
one_line: Standalone handheld RFID/NFC reader (LCD, nav switch, swappable antennas, microSD) that identifies, saves, loads, clones to T5577, emulates and brute-forces HID/EM4100/Mifare tags untethered. Configuration options ranged $55-$400, so no single price recorded.
why_notable: A separate commercial Proxmark line from a different vendor than the RRG/Iceman hardware behind the tracked models - needs a human check against the existing Proxmark entries.

name: BusKill
one_line: Magnetic breakaway USB cable acting as a laptop dead-man's switch: yanked away, it triggers a configured action - screen lock, shutdown, or on Linux an optional LUKS-header wipe.
why_notable: Anti-seizure gadget for snatch-and-run and border-search scenarios; different mechanism from the tracked USBKill V4, which destroys the port electrically.

name: Ovrdrive USB
one_line: Open-hardware 8GB USB drive (ATtiny24A + SM3257ENT) reading as blank storage unless plugged in three times in quick succession; includes a disabled-by-default circuit that can invert supply voltage to overheat the flash chip as a physical self-destruct.
why_notable: Anti-forensics hidden-data storage with an explicit hardware self-destruct hook.

name: UsbSafe2
one_line: Inline USB dongle with a physical button to disable the data lines (anti-juice-jacking) and clamp output voltage/current at five selectable thresholds to protect the downstream device from a malicious or faulty host.
why_notable: Data blocker plus overvoltage/overcurrent cutoff; same niche as the tracked O.MG UnBlocker but a distinct older product.

name: unsurv offline
one_line: ESP32 board with GNSS receiver, accelerometer and NFC tag interface that cross-references logged GPS tracks against an offline OpenStreetMap database of camera locations, producing a daily surveillance-camera proximity report read out over NFC.
why_notable: Counter-surveillance camera-proximity logger; the automotive/forensics survey judged it out of scope as a privacy receiver, the Crowd Supply survey included it. Needs a call.

name: QuadRF
one_line: 4x4 coherent MIMO SDR tile with an integrated Raspberry Pi 5 that measures arrival-time differences across four antennas to render a real-time AR overlay of RF sources on a camera feed at 30fps, and can pass a selected signal to GNU Radio.
why_notable: Vendor names locating hidden wireless cameras and rogue access points through walls; RF direction-finding in the same spirit as the tracked KrakenSDR.

name: moRFeus
one_line: Field-configurable 30MHz-6GHz frequency mixer/converter and signal generator with an LCD and button interface and USB-HID programmability, switching between mixer and standalone generator modes.
why_notable: Long-standing RF-hacking accessory for shifting HackRF/SDR tuning ranges. Vendor's own use-case list names wideband jammers, though the device is general-purpose lab gear.

name: Sword of Secrets
one_line: Keychain-sized RISC-V board hosting a multi-stage hardware CTF requiring hardware reverse engineering, breaching protection registers over SPI/UART and firmware-level exploitation; new stages arrive as USB firmware updates.
why_notable: Hands-on hardware-hacking training device (successor to The Skull CTF) built on real embedded-exploitation technique. Training targets are a category nothing tracked covers.

name: GlitchCaster
one_line: Modular EMFI probe head based on the open PicoEMP design generating a roughly 250V EM pulse through a leaded or SMA probe coil; standard 40mm-fan mounting so it can be positioned by a 3D-printer or CNC stage. No built-in controller.
why_notable: Commercial EMFI tool on the same open design as the tracked ChipSHOUTER-PicoEMP, aimed at CNC-mounted repeatable glitching. Coming Soon - no funding, no price.

name: EPIC Erebus
one_line: M.2 2230 FPGA board (Lattice ECP5) for PCIe DMA research; PCILeech-compatible, supports standalone memory acquisition and patch/match without a tethered host, fully open gateware, firmware and toolchain.
why_notable: Compact PCILeech-class DMA board in M.2 form factor, distinct from the tracked Screamer PCIe Squirrel. Coming Soon - not yet funded, no price.

name: ChipJabber Unplugged
one_line: DIY-buildable voltage fault-injection kit with no programmable logic, in three build variants (through-hole, small SMD battery-powered Mini, and home-etch/PCB-mill friendly); pairs with a NOTDuino target demonstrating bypass of an EEPROM-keyed secure-boot check.
why_notable: Manual knob-tuned glitcher rather than an automated FPGA one - distinct from ChipWhisperer-Lite/Nano/Husky. Coming Soon, no price.

name: RFGEN44
one_line: USB-powered driver-free RF signal generator (ADF4351 synthesizer, PIC16 MCU) producing 35MHz-4.4GHz output in 10kHz steps, controllable over USB HID from Python or Matlab. Live crowdfunding campaign.
why_notable: Generic hobbyist/lab RF source with no security framing on its page; included only for dual-use potential. Weakest candidate in this batch.

name: HackyPi
one_line: RP2040 USB stick with a 1.14in TFT and SD slot that emulates HID keyboard input and runs drag-and-drop cross-platform payload scripts.
why_notable: BadUSB board with an onboard display - not one of the tracked Digispark/CH552/pico-ducky designs.

name: USB Snake Box
one_line: CircuitPython microcontroller in a 3D-printed box with four buttons, each mapped to a different pre-programmed keystroke-injection payload.
why_notable: Multi-button physical BadUSB, a distinct form factor from tracked single-payload devices.

name: BLE BadUSB (JDY-08)
one_line: ATmega32U4 + JDY-08 BLE module USB stick emulating keyboard and mouse and accepting remote command injection over BLE 4.0; open source, Arduino-programmable.
why_notable: BLE-remote-triggered BadUSB - a different attack surface from the Wi-Fi and onboard-payload devices tracked.

name: BLE BadUSB (JDY-10)
one_line: Same design as the JDY-08 variant with a JDY-10 BLE module.
why_notable: Near-duplicate SKU of the JDY-08 board, differing only in the BLE radio module. Probably one record with a variant note.

name: Wifi BadUSB
one_line: ATmega32U4 + ESP-12F USB stick acting as a HID injector and hosting its own Wi-Fi access point for control and reflashing; runs supremeDuck, wifi_ducky or ESPloitV2.
why_notable: Wi-Fi-controlled BadUSB from the same maker, distinct hardware from the BLE variants.

name: Vidar attiny85 based BadUSB
one_line: Miniature ATtiny85 USB stick emulating a keyboard and firing a pre-programmed payload on plug-in; firmware user-modifiable.
why_notable: Minimal cheap ATtiny85 BadUSB from a different maker than the tracked Digispark/CH552 boards.

name: Programmable BadUSB Payload Cable USB-A to USB-C
one_line: USB-A to USB-C cable with an embedded microcontroller emulating HID and mass storage, storing multiple reprogrammable payloads, with an LED status indicator.
why_notable: Cable-form payload injector at a tenth the price of an O.MG Cable - worth comparing directly against it.

name: Masterkey - WiFi USB Keylogger
one_line: Inline USB pass-through that logs keystrokes internally, exposes a Wi-Fi AP for wireless retrieval, and can also inject keystrokes and scripts.
why_notable: Combined hardware keylogger and HID injector from the ESP32 Marauder author.

name: KEYVILBOARD - Wi-Fi
one_line: Inline hardware keylogger for QWERTY keyboards storing about 3M characters, retrievable over a hidden Wi-Fi network at up to 30m range; supports remote key injection.
why_notable: Distinct Wi-Fi-exfil keylogger, different maker and hardware from Masterkey and the tracked AirDrive.

name: Odiin: NFC Tag Emulation Toolkit
one_line: nRF52840 handheld with a 320x240 LCD that loads tag dump files from SD and emulates NFC-A tags (NTAG21X, partial MIFARE Classic/Ultralight) when tapped to a reader.
why_notable: Dedicated NFC tag-emulation handheld, distinct from the tracked Chameleon, ACR122U and Proxmark devices.

name: PicoGlitcher v3
one_line: Raspberry Pi Pico 2 voltage-glitching tool with two MOSFET crowbar outputs, 1.2-5V level shifters and adjustable trigger filtering for fault injection against microcontrollers.
why_notable: Same product as the GitHub fault-injection-library / Findus entry, at $59 here versus a ~$67 estimate from the vendor's own store - resolve before publishing.

name: hs-probe
one_line: STM32F723 open-hardware SWD/JTAG probe, CMSIS-DAP v1/v2 compatible, USB 2.0 High-Speed with a USB mux for bootloader access; ships with ribbon cables and STDC10/14 connectors.
why_notable: Open high-speed debug probe from the probe-rs project, distinct from the tracked Bus Pirate, Glasgow and Tigard.

name: XDS110 Debugger
one_line: Compact USB debug probe for TI MCUs and DSPs supporting JTAG, cJTAG, SWD and UART with 5V/3.3V target power; works with CCS, Keil and OpenOCD.
why_notable: Cheap dedicated probe for TI silicon, a niche the tracked general-purpose probes do not cover.

name: IBDAP - CMSIS-DAP JTAG/SWD Debug Adapter
one_line: NXP LPC11U35 open-source USB debug adapter implementing CMSIS-DAP over JTAG/SWD with UART/I2C/SPI peripherals for breakpoints, stepping and firmware download to ARM targets.
why_notable: Independent open-hardware JTAG/SWD adapter.

name: Mini DAPLink Debug Probe
one_line: 3.2x1.7cm USB-C DAPLink probe for ARM Cortex-M targets (STM32, GD32, nRF51/52) over SWD/JTAG plus a USB-serial UART bridge; enumerates as COM port and HID.
why_notable: Extremely cheap dedicated SWD/JTAG probe - the budget end of the debug-probe comparison.

name: Open Source Portable USB Sniffer USB2.0
one_line: Board capturing USB 1.1/2.0 bus traffic at up to 48Mbps with open-source capture firmware and four status LEDs; captures analyzed in Wireshark.
why_notable: Dedicated USB protocol-analysis hardware, a niche not represented.

name: tinySniffer - USB sniffer
one_line: Inline pass-through capturing full USB 1.x/2.0 enumeration and traffic between host and peripheral, remotely controllable, with disconnect/reconnect simulation and capture filtering.
why_notable: Remote-operable inline USB sniffer intended to be shipped to a target site - a different use case from bench analyzers.

name: LittlePcap Network Tap
one_line: Inline dual-gigabit-Ethernet tap writing captured traffic as PCAP files directly to an attached USB drive; USB-C powered, roughly 16s boot.
why_notable: Captures to its own USB drive, unlike the tracked Throwing Star and Plunder Bug which need a separate capture host.

name: Negotchi - network security scanner
one_line: ESP8266 + OLED board that periodically scans the local Wi-Fi network for hosts and vulnerabilities and runs a honeypot service, sounding an on-screen alarm if the honeypot is touched.
why_notable: Standalone intrusion-detection gadget - a different category from the tracked wardriving and deauth boards.

name: Netgotchi Pro
one_line: Battery-powered ESP8266 + OLED variant of Negotchi with the same scanning, honeypot and alarm functions, configurable by onboard buttons or a phone web portal.
why_notable: Portable version of the same maker's scanner line.

name: ESP32 Network Toolbox
one_line: ESP32 board with an Android companion app: Wi-Fi scanning, promiscuous packet sniffing, deauth frames, evil-twin captive portal, network mapping and BLE scanning, exporting PCAP/CSV/JSON.
why_notable: Full Wi-Fi pentest toolbox with a phone app. Listing shows out of stock since Aug 2023 - supply needs checking.

name: DSTIKE Deauther32 Ultra
one_line: Dual-MCU handheld (ESP32-S3 + ESP32-C5) with two 1.54in colour displays, dual antennas and a 3-cell 18650 battery; the S3 side does 2.4GHz scanning, the C5 side adds 2.4/5GHz Wi-Fi 6 scanning and deauth.
why_notable: Same maker as the tracked DSTIKE Deauther Watch but a non-watch dual-band flagship. 5GHz capability the tracked Marauder boards lack.

name: ESP32 Marauder Double Barrel 5G - C5 version
one_line: Dual-system board: a standalone ESP32 Marauder unit with touchscreen, battery and GPS, plus a second ESP32-C5 dual-band 2.4/5GHz Flipper-controlled radio, a CC1101 sub-GHz chip and four external antennas.
why_notable: Adds genuine 5GHz Wi-Fi scanning and deauth, which the tracked Marauder v6.1/v7/v8 boards do not have.

name: 2.4/5 GHz Deauther
one_line: RTL8720dn board hosting its own AP with a web UI, scanning and deauthing across 2.4GHz and 5GHz, with an RGB status LED.
why_notable: Dual-band deauther on an RTL8720dn rather than ESP32/ESP8266 - a different chipset from every tracked deauther. Listing marked Product Retired with no price.

name: Esp8266 WIFI Deauther
one_line: ESP8266 board hosting an open Wi-Fi network and a web control interface at 192.168.4.1 for deauth testing.
why_notable: Basic independent ESP8266 deauther.

name: Wifi deauther PLUG PLAY ESP8266 v2.0
one_line: Pre-flashed NodeMCU with a web deauther UI at 192.168.4.1 supporting SSID spoofing, probe-request spam and deauthentication, powered over micro-USB.
why_notable: Pre-flashed NodeMCU reseller listing.

name: NetNinja Wardriving GPS Marauder
one_line: Flipper Zero expansion combining an ESP32 with a battery-backed GPS module and 2.4GHz antenna, writing geotagged Wi-Fi PCAPs to the Flipper's SD card, preloaded with Marauder.
why_notable: GPS-tagged wardriving for Flipper Zero, a capability the tracked Flipper Wi-Fi boards lack.

name: Flipper Zero Wardriving GPS enabled ESP32 Board
one_line: ESP32 with external antenna and GPS receiver as a Flipper Zero add-on, preloaded with Marauder, in a 3D-printed case; connects over serial and logs to the Flipper SD card.
why_notable: Same concept as NetNinja from a different maker at a $20 premium - a direct head-to-head comparison.

name: MSI.SDR 10kHz-2GHz Panadapter SDR Receiver
one_line: 12-bit ADC SDR receiver covering 10kHz-2GHz with up to 10MHz bandwidth, 0.5ppm TCXO, SMA antenna port, micro-USB, aluminium enclosure.
why_notable: Wideband receiver in a different product line from the tracked RTL-SDR, HackRF, KrakenSDR and PlutoSDR. An RSP1 clone - worth stating plainly.

name: SDR-Rx Up Converter Module
one_line: HF upconverter and preamp (10kHz-50MHz, relay-switched VHF/UHF/SHF pass-through) extending the low-frequency range of an existing RTL-SDR dongle; F and BNC connectors, USB powered.
why_notable: Adds real HF reception to existing SDR dongles but is an accessory rather than a standalone tool.

name: RTL-SDR Receiver w/ TCXO & Bias-T
one_line: RTL2832U + R820T2 dongle (500kHz-1.7GHz) with TCXO and software-controlled bias-tee for powering external antennas or LNAs, aluminium enclosure.
why_notable: Same product class as the tracked RTL-SDR Blog V4 from a different manufacturer, at nearly double the price - a useful cautionary comparison.

name: VICINO
one_line: ST25R3916B RFID/NFC reader-writer module over SPI, pin- and mounting-hole-compatible with existing RC522 project designs.
why_notable: Higher-end RFID chipset than the common cheap MFRC522 boards, positioned as a drop-in upgrade.

name: NFC Card Reader Module with ESP32-S3
one_line: ESP32-S3 + PN5321 module reading, writing and emulating ISO14443 A/B, MIFARE and FeliCa, with an 8-LED array, 3W speaker and microSD for audio-visual feedback on tag events.
why_notable: Full read/write/emulate NFC chipset on an ESP32-S3, though the listing frames it as an access-control project board rather than a pentest tool.

name: ESPboy:DIY
one_line: ESP8266 handheld (128x128 TFT, 8 buttons, speaker, battery) marketed for retro gaming, with plug-in modules and firmware for Wi-Fi attacks, RFID/NFC cloning and emulation, iButton storage, 433MHz barrier control, U2F and BadUSB payloads.
why_notable: Genuine multi-protocol capability bolted onto a retro-gaming platform - borderline because gaming is the primary marketed use.

name: Flipper Zero WiFi Multiboard NRF24+ESP32
one_line: Flipper Zero add-on with a switch selecting between an nRF24 module for packet sniffing and mousejacking and an ESP32 module for Wi-Fi/Marauder, over a single USB connection.
why_notable: Similar to the tracked Flipper 3-in-1 Multi Board but without the CC1101 sub-GHz radio, at a higher price.

name: Evil Crow Cable
one_line: ATtiny85 BadUSB cable with data lines enabled, emulating a keyboard to run pre-programmed payloads. No Wi-Fi.
why_notable: Same brand as the tracked Evil Crow Cable Wind but genuinely different silicon - ATtiny85 with no ESP32-S3 or Wi-Fi, at half the price.

name: EvilCrowCable-Wind USB-A to Type-C
one_line: ESP32-S3 BadUSB cable (USB-A to USB-C) emulating keyboard HID and hosting a Wi-Fi control panel; open-source firmware.
why_notable: Connector-variant SKU of the tracked Evil Crow Cable Wind.

name: HacPhone - Rooted NetHunter/Kali Nexus 5X
one_line: Rooted Nexus 5X pre-installed with Kali NetHunter for Wi-Fi cracking and deauth, network recon, vulnerability testing and Bluetooth/NFC assessment.
why_notable: A discontinued retail phone re-flashed and sold as a pentest platform - base hardware is old retail, but the security firmware is the product.

name: Firewalla
one_line: Inline network appliance (quad-core ARM, 512MB RAM) between router and LAN, passively monitoring connected devices for threats, filtering content and offering VPN and ad-blocking through a mobile app.
why_notable: Consumer defensive appliance rather than a testing tool - weakest fit in this batch. Recommend dropping.

name: PicoEMP PCB Board ONLY
one_line: Unpopulated bare PCB for the open-source PicoEMP electromagnetic fault-injection tool; components not included, DIY assembly required.
why_notable: Bare-PCB option for the tracked ChipSHOUTER-PicoEMP design - in scope per the DIY-only decision, and the cheapest entry into EMFI at $7.

name: Chamele0n Ultra reseller listing
one_line: nRF52840 keychain reading and writing HF and LF RFID/IC cards and emulating up to 8 stored tags standalone, over BLE or USB.
why_notable: Reseller listing of tracked hardware; useful only as a price data point ($45).

name: Bruce Cardputer reseller listing
one_line: ESP32-S3 handheld with keyboard and display preloaded with Bruce firmware: Python scripts, RFID/NFC scanning, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth testing, USB payload automation.
why_notable: Reseller of the tracked M5Stack Cardputer + Bruce combination; price data point only.

name: ESP32 CYD Launcher Build
one_line: ESP32-2432S028R Cheap Yellow Display board in a 3D-printed case preloaded with launcher firmware to switch between Marauder, Bruce, Ghost ESP and others without reflashing; includes SD card, cables and stylus.
why_notable: Tracked board packaged with a multi-firmware launcher - the launcher concept itself may deserve a note on the CYD record.
